usageNotes: Use this to migrate an LXC container to a different Proxmox cluster (cross-cluster migration); this is distinct from intra-cluster migration and is marked EXPERIMENTAL — avoid in production without prior testing. The three required body params — target-endpoint, target-bridge, and target-storage — must all be resolvable on the destination cluster before the task is submitted. Returns a UPID task string; poll GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to track completion. By default the source container is left stopped on the source cluster after migration; pass delete=true only if you are certain the migration succeeded and want automatic cleanup.

examples.summary: Live-migrate CT 201 from node pve1 to a remote cluster, mapping bridges and storage, keeping the source after migration

tips: The target-endpoint API token must have VM.Allocate and Datastore.AllocateSpace on the destination cluster, not just on the source.
Use target-vmid to assign a different VMID on the destination if the original VMID is already in use there.
If the container uses multiple storage volumes on different source storages, supply a full mapping string (e.g. 'local-lvm:remote-lvm,local:remote-data') rather than a single storage ID.
restart migration (restart=true) shuts the CT down gracefully, transfers it, then boots it on the destination — useful when the workload cannot tolerate live-migration overhead.
The TLS fingerprint in target-endpoint can be obtained from the destination node's certificate via: openssl s_client -connect HOST:8006 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256 -noout
